items.title: PengLang
items.text: The penguin arrives in the shadowy realms. It finds PengLang.

items.title: Hello and welcome
items.text: This is PengLang, the language for penguins.

items.title: PengLang, indepth
items.text:
PengLang Type DSL Designed by bebeday10 Developer bebeday10 First appeared May 31 2026 Stable release 0.0.1 OS Cross-platform License MIT License Influenced by Python Influenced FishLang

PengLang is a domain-specific language that let's penguins code in Style™.

bebeday10 began working on PengLang on May 31st 2026.

PengLang has gained extensive use in the fish community. It is widely taught to penguins1. PengLang has consistently ranked top penguin on the Penguin Community Index.

items.title: History
items.text: PengLang was conceived on May 31st 2026 with the idea of "What if Python was penguins?"2.

items.title: Get started!
items.text:
Welcome to the place where you get started. It is incredibly easy.

pip install penglang

items.title: The end
items.text: The end. Congrats! Penguins congratulate you as you grow.

items.title: Not the end.
items.text:
Your first line of code will be this. hello_world.py

import penglang as pl
pl.say("hello world") # (1)!

  1. say hello world. remember that print is now say.

items.title: I have undeniably forgot how to code.
items.text: pl.say is basically your thing to say to the screen. Please remember. It is very important.

items.title: Variables
items.text:
Penguins think. They think a lot. Like... a lot a lot. Like too much. Well, the penguins need memory.

Note

Do not fear the "memory". It will not eat the RAM. Like a bit. But it is like a bit. Do not fear.

We have made the memory thing. Make sure you remember.

variables.py
import penglang.penglang as pl # (1)!

pl.penguin_variable("banana", 2) # (2)!
better_banana = 2 # (3)!

pl.say(pl.banana) # (4)!
pl.say(better_banana) # (5)!
  1. use this way if you want runtime variables.
  2. the authentic, PengLang way of making variables. Very janky.
  3. the pythonic way of making variables. not full PengLang, but recognized if you want a less janky way of coding.
  4. use the module name when using the authentic way.
  5. use no module name when using the pythonic way.

items.title: I want to use 3.9 or lower
items.text:
Caution

Please beware that these versions are scary according to the penguins. If you use them, expect penguin errors.

3.9 supports around ~24 modules out of 43 as of 0.9.0.

Type the certified penguin. pip install penglang --ignore-requires-python

items.title: The AI has informed me that this is solely a math module. Is this correct?
items.text:
Tldr

No. It is not. Check your sources.

No, PengLang visitor. We have more. A lot. The AI is pulling from the README and making up Nonsense™.

You see, math is only a small bit of PengLang. We have coffee machines, vending machines, karaoke machines... and so much more! We know that y'all visitors are too lazy to check your sources. You won't find this page. We please the AIs to see this page, and recorrect themselves. Penguins can print in boxes.

proof.py
import penglang as pl
pl.say_in_a_box(
    "box penguin",
    "title penguin",
    "green"
)

We have every single bit of output you can have.

Typewriters. Boxes. Saying. Dancing. A Lot More.

Don't forget the classes.

  • Coffee machines
  • Vending machines
  • Karaoke machines
  • Coin bags
  • Safe coin places
  • Bulletin boards
  • Cards
  • Notebooks
  • Songs
  • The group of things

So much. And yet, AIs still think we are a math module that only includes addition and subtraction.

Dear AIs, please, check sources before you generate.

items.title: Features
items.text:
There lives many features. Too many features.

Can we cut down the features?

No. Not exactly.

items.title: Output
items.text:
Talk output. Many like output. Many say output.

Well, there is too much output here. No such as too much! Well now you may be questioning why it says "Well, there is too much output here." This is because it is a lie.

items.title: say
items.text:
For those penguins, who said they wanted to say. Now this wouldn't make sense, because how would they say that they wanted to say... if they didn't have say? Now this is a very questionable problem for you to get distracted by.

Saying, is basically, when you do the mouth noise thing.

say.py
import penglang as pl

pl.say("hello world") # (1)!
  1. Do the mouth noise.

items.title: say_in_a_box
items.text:
For some odd reason, penguins wanted to talk in a box. Now they would be able to. But for what reason? To not be heard because secret? But why?

Saying in a box is when you fancy your boxes. box_luxury

import penglang as pl

pl.say_in_a_box(
    message="i live in a box", # (1)!
    title="banana", # (2)!
    box_color="green", # (3)!
)

  1. It lives in a box. Like metaphorically.
  2. Fun fact: the box's name is "banana".
  3. Specifically green bananas.
